facts.text: The John Deere Pavilion in Moline showcases a living history of Midwest farming, displaying plows, tractors, and combines from past to present.
Moline, once called “Plow City,” remains the world headquarters for John Deere, keeping farm implements as its primary economic driver.
The city’s original layout was a neat grid of sixteen square blocks, with streets named after the landowners who first owned the land.
Moline sits at the confluence of the Rock and Mississippi rivers, a geographic feature that helped shape its early industrial boom.
In the 1840s, a factory town called “Rock Island Mills” sprang up on the Illinois shore, sparking rapid growth along the riverbank.
The first transcontinental railroad was routed through Moline, connecting the region to the national economy and ending its isolation.
